title: The machines and the prompts
target: What the shop's computer and tablet are, and where the game's own prompts and hints come from, so the two halves of the interface can be told apart.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A computer or tablet in the shop

steps.do: Treat the shop's computer as an object in the room before it is a menu.
steps.because: the computer is an object with an interaction of its own (Computer, ComputerInteraction)

steps.do: Expect the screens to belong to a system with a desktop of its own.
steps.because: it runs a system of its own, with a desktop (ComputerOperatingSystem, GenericDesktop)

steps.do: Know that the tablet is a device of its own rather than the same machine.
steps.because: the game has a tablet device of its own and the tablet carries a cart item (TabletDevice, TabletCartItem)

steps.do: Look at the tablet's own art rather than assuming it shares the computer's.
steps.because: the game ships a texture for the tablet and a scanner icon for it (T_Tablet_AlbedoTransparency, TabletScannerIcon)

steps.do: Follow an online order as a customer rather than as a line in a list.
steps.because: orders bring customers that are generated, shown on the map and kept in a networked form (OnlineOrderCustomerGenerator, OnlineOrderCustomerMapItem, NetworkOnlineOrderCustomer)

steps.do: Read hints as the game's own system rather than as part of the machine.
steps.because: interaction hints are handled by a manager of their own and the game runs a ping system of its own (InteractionHintsManager, PingSystem)

steps.do: Expect the tool wheel and the keys to have prompts of their own.
steps.because: the tool wheel has a handler for its input hint, and key icons are managed with kinds of their own (ToolWheelInputHintHandler, KeyIconManager, KeyDisplayType)

steps.do: Know that a prompt can be chosen because the interaction has a type.
steps.because: an interaction and the thing interacted with each carry a type (InteractionType, InteractactableType)

commonMistakes: Looking for the tablet's screens on the computer.
Hunting in menus for something the prompt system is already telling you.
Reading an online order as a delivery rather than as a customer.
Assuming every machine in the shop draws its prompts the same way.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
